Sue Lines I will now deal with the amendments moved by Senator Bell. _One Nation's circulated amendments—_ (1) Clause 2, page 2 (after table item 4), insert: (2) Schedule 2, page 22 (after line 12), at the end of the Schedule, add: Part 3 — Meaning of hors de combat _Criminal Code Act 1995_ 9 Dictionary in the _Criminal Code_ (definition of _hors de combat_ ) Repeal the definition, substitute: _hors de combat_: a person is _hors de combat_ if: (a) the person is in the power of an adverse party; and (b) the person: (i) clearly expresses an intention to surrender; or (ii) has been rendered unconscious or is otherwise incapacitated by wounds or sickness and is therefore incapable of defending himself or herself; and (c) the person abstains from any hostile act and does not attempt to escape. 10 Application provision (1) The definition of _hors de combat_ in the Dictionary in the _Criminal Code_, as inserted by this Part, applies in relation to: (a) any conduct engaged in on or after 26 September 2002; and (b) any legal proceedings that are commenced on or after that day, if the proceedings have not been finally determined before the commencement of this item. (2) In this item, _legal proceedings_ include any proceedings before a court or tribunal, and include proceedings that are pending. The question is that the amendments on 3897 be agreed to.

Sue Lines I will now deal with the amendments circulated by the Australian Greens on sheet 3791. The question is that schedule 2 stand as printed. _The Australian Greens' circulated amendments—_ (2) Schedule 2, page 16 (line 1) to page 22 (line 12), to be opposed.

Sue Lines As that matter was resolved in the affirmative, the consequential amendment on sheet 3791 will not be put. The question now is that the remaining stages of the bill be agreed to and the bill be now passed.

Moved the Crimes and Other Legislation Amendment (Omnibus No. 1) Bill 2026, which would modernise police powers, criminal prosecutions, federal prosecution, extradition and telecommunications laws while retaining safeguards and procedural fairness.

Ordered that the Export Control Amendment (Clarifying Obligations Relating to Registered Establishments) Bill 2026 and the Crimes and Other Legislation Amendment (Omnibus No. 1) Bill 2026 be referred to the Federation Chamber for further consideration after debate on each second-reading motion is adjourned.

Supported the Crimes and Other Legislation Amendment (Omnibus No. 1) Bill 2026 in the House but called for Senate committee scrutiny, arguing that its extension of cybercrime disruption powers to 4 September 2029 should not substitute for broader electronic surveillance reform.

Argued that the Crimes and Other Legislation Amendment (Omnibus No. 1) Bill 2026 would modernise crime, drug, prosecution and extradition laws, extend specified warrants to 2029, and improve law-enforcement efficiency while retaining safeguards; the second-reading question remained unresolved and the bill was returned for further consideration.

Supported the Crimes and Other Legislation Amendment (Omnibus No.1) Bill 2026 while proposing parliamentary review of expanded extradition arrest powers and seeking clarification on Director of Public Prosecutions changes, accepting technical reforms but criticising the removal of ACIC data disruption warrant powers and the delayed modernisation of electronic surveillance laws; other contributions raised concerns about drug thresholds and vulnerable defendants.

Asked whether the CDPP's previous work with the Office of the Special Investigator created an actual, potential or perceived conflict in prosecuting Ben Roberts-Smith; the minister said the director saw no conflict, the Attorney-General did not accept one existed, and amended provisions would improve conflict management while current safeguards remained.

Moved amendments to bring forward to 1 July 2027 the sunset date for account takeover, data disruption and network activity warrants, seeking a public interest monitor and stronger safeguards; the government opposed the amendments pending broader reforms, the coalition supported retaining the powers until 4 September 2029, and questions on conflicts of interest were taken on notice.

As President, put to a vote amendments to the Crimes and Other Legislation Amendment (Omnibus No. 1) Bill 2026, including a Greens amendment to bring forward sunset dates in schedule 1 from September 2029 to July 2027 and a One Nation amendment restoring an earlier definition of 'hors de combat' in the Criminal Code, before the bill passed.
